message.reasoning:
We need to fix compilation errors. The test class uses JUnit 4 annotations (@Test, @Before, @After, etc.) but also JUnit 5 annotations (@Nested, @DisplayName, @BeforeAll, @BeforeEach, @AfterAll, @ExtendWith). The environment likely only has JUnit 4. So we should replace JUnit 5 annotations with JUnit 4 equivalents, and remove Mockito imports if not available. Alternatively, we can add imports for JUnit 5, but the compilation errors indicate missing packages for junit.jupiter.api.extension, etc. So easiest: rewrite test class to use only JUnit 4. Also remove Mockito usage, or replace with simple stub. Since we have a ConstantNumIndicator stub, we can avoid mocking. The tests that use mock and verify can be simplified or removed. However we need to keep functionality. Could replace mock with a simple stub indicator that returns constant value and tracks calls. For verification, we can just assert values.

Also many duplicate imports and missing ConstantIndicator generic type inference. ConstantIndicator likely defined as ConstantIndicator<T extends Num>. The constructor expects a Num value; we need to specify type parameter: new ConstantIndicator<Num>(DecimalNum.valueOf(2)). Or maybe ConstantIndicator<Num>. So fix those.

Also ConstantNumIndicator implements Indicator<Num> but must implement getUnstableBars() method (abstract). Need to add that method returning 0.

Similarly anonymous Indicator in indicatorReturningNullValues test needs getUnstableBars.

Also highest indicator expects Indicator<Num> not BarSeries; HighestValueIndicator constructor likely takes Indicator<Num> and int. Actually in ta4j, HighestValueIndicator(Indicator<Num> indicator, int timeFrame). But they passed BarSeries. Should use new HighestValueIndicator(new ClosePriceIndicator(hvSeries), 2). So fix.

Also mismatched series length test expects IndexOutOfBoundsException; but NumericIndicator multiplication may check series length; we can keep.

Also different BarSeries handling test expects IllegalArgumentException when series differ; may be already thrown.

Also null delegate indicator test: NumericIndicator.of(null) will cause NPE earlier; but they expect later NPE on getValue. Could keep.

Also constantTimesConstant tests duplicated; fine.

We need to import JUnit 4: org.junit.Test, org.junit.Before, org.junit.After, org.junit.BeforeClass, org.junit.AfterClass, org.junit.Assert.*. Also for nested groups we can just use inner classes with @RunWith(Enclosed.class) maybe. JUnit 4 supports @RunWith(Enclosed.class) to have nested test classes. So we can add @RunWith(Enclosed.class) at top, and annotate nested classes with @RunWith(Enclosed.class)? Actually Enclosed runs inner static classes as separate test classes. So we need inner static classes. The current nested classes are non-static. We'll convert them to static inner classes and annotate outer class with @RunWith(Enclosed.class). Also need @BeforeClass, @AfterClass for static setup/teardown.

Simplify: we can drop nested grouping and just have all tests in the same class; easier. Remove inner classes and merge tests. But many tests rely on grouping; we can just keep them as separate @Test methods. Simpler: remove inner classes and related annotations.

Thus produce a cleaned test class using JUnit 4 only, no Mockito, no JUnit5.

Implement constant indicator generic: new ConstantIndicator<Num>(DecimalNum.valueOf(...))

Implement stub ConstantNumIndicator implements getUnstableBars returning 0.

Implement simple constant stub for mock test: we can reuse ConstantNumIndicator.

Remove mock verification.

Remove @DisplayName annotations.

Remove @ExtendWith.

Remove imports for JUnit5, Mockito, etc.

Add necessary imports.

Now ensure NumericIndicator.of works with Indicator<Num>.

Also need to import org.junit.runner.RunWith and Enclosed if we keep nested.

Simplify: keep all tests as top-level methods, no nested.

We'll produce final corrected code.
